tool_summary: Installs, upgrades, and removes Node.js packages. Runs arbitrary package lifecycle scripts (preinstall, postinstall, etc.) by default.
platform_notes: npm behavior and flags are consistent across Linux and macOS.

rules.description: The --registry flag points npm at a package registry other than the default. Installing from an untrusted or unfamiliar registry is a common supply-chain attack vector, since npm runs package lifecycle scripts (postinstall, etc.) by default at install time with the invoking user's privileges.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be uninstalled, but its lifecycle scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: Installing directly from a git URL or a tarball URL bypasses the registry entirely, fetching and executing code from a source that has not gone through any registry review or the installed-package audit npm otherwise applies.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be uninstalled, but lifecycle scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: Installs a package. By default npm executes lifecycle scripts (preinstall, install, postinstall) declared in the package's package.json with the invoking user's privileges, at install time.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be uninstalled, but lifecycle scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: The run/run-script subcommand executes an arbitrary script defined in package.json's scripts field. The script's content is not inspected by commandant.
rules.reversible_note: Reversibility depends entirely on the script's contents, which commandant does not inspect.

rules.description: Manages Node.js packages. Read-only subcommands (list, view, search, outdated) do not alter system state. Severity here reflects that unrecognized or future npm subcommands fall through to this rule; known read-only subcommands are not themselves being flagged as risky.
rules.notes: Default bumped to WARNING (not INFO) because this tool's CLI surface evolves quickly; an unmatched/unrecognized subcommand should surface for review rather than silently pass as benign.
